name: Mythopoetic men's movement
summary: The mythopoetic men's movement was an American self-help movement of the 1980s and 1990s, led by Robert Bly, Robert Moore, Douglas Gillette and Michael Meade, that used myth, fairy tale and Jungian archetypes in workshops and retreats to restore a 'deep masculine' it saw as lost with the decline of initiation and the absent father. It treats masculine and feminine as rooted in inherited archetypes, blames both immature patriarchy and a feminised culture for men's wounds, and mostly avoids explicit political programmes.
scope: The movement as defined by its leaders' texts (Moore and Gillette, s1) and the scholarship on it (s2, s3). It excludes the pro-feminist and men's rights strands of the wider men's movement, and later groups such as the ManKind Project.
